subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In Christian belief, the Last Judgement is when:
options: The Bible was finally completed
God judges people and decides their eternal destiny
Jesus was put on trial by Pilate
People choose their own religion
questions.explain: At the Last Judgement Christians believe God will judge all people, leading to heaven or hell.

questions.q: In Christian teaching, the term 'free will' refers to the belief that humans:
options: Can never choose to sin
Are forced by God to do good
Are able to choose between right and wrong
Have no responsibility for their actions
questions.explain: Free will is the God-given ability to choose between good and evil, making humans responsible for their choices.

questions.q: The Ascension in Christianity refers to Jesus:
options: Being baptised in the Jordan
Returning to God the Father in heaven
Being born in Bethlehem
Calming the storm
questions.explain: The Ascension is Jesus returning to heaven to be with God the Father after his resurrection.

questions.q: For many Christians, purgatory (taught especially in Roman Catholicism) is:
options: A festival celebrated in spring
A state of cleansing before entering heaven
The place where Jesus was buried
Another name for hell
questions.explain: In Catholic teaching, purgatory is a state of purification for the soul before entering heaven.

questions.q: The Parable of the Good Samaritan mainly teaches Christians to:
options: Travel to Jerusalem on pilgrimage
Become priests or Levites
Only help people from their own community
Show love and care to anyone in need
questions.explain: The parable teaches that a true neighbour shows compassion to anyone in need, regardless of background.

questions.q: In Christian belief, original sin describes:
options: The first sin a person commits as an adult
The sinful tendency humans inherit, traced to Adam and Eve's disobedience
The most serious crime in society
A sin that can never be forgiven
questions.explain: Original sin is the human tendency to sin that Christians trace back to Adam and Eve's fall.

questions.q: Christians believe Jesus is 'fully human and fully divine'. This idea is central to the:
options: Ascension
Incarnation
Sermon on the Mount
Last Supper
questions.explain: The Incarnation teaches that in Jesus, God became fully human while remaining fully divine.

questions.q: When Jesus was asked for the greatest commandment, he taught that people should:
options: Give all their money to the poor
Keep the Sabbath above all else
Love God and love your neighbour as yourself
Avoid eating certain foods
questions.explain: Jesus summarised the law as loving God with all your heart and loving your neighbour as yourself.

questions.q: The Incarnation is the Christian belief that:
options: Jesus rose from the dead
Jesus went up to heaven
God became human in the person of Jesus
Souls are reborn into new bodies
questions.explain: The Incarnation is the belief that God took on human form as Jesus Christ.

questions.q: Many Christians believe heaven is best described as:
options: Eternal life in the presence of God
A reward for being rich
A temporary stopping point before rebirth
A place only for clergy
questions.explain: Christians generally see heaven as eternal life lived in the presence of God.

questions.q: In the Christian creation account in Genesis, God creates the universe:
options: By accident over millions of years
With the help of other gods
From the body of a defeated enemy
Through his word, out of nothing
questions.explain: Genesis describes God creating the world deliberately through his word, out of nothing.

questions.q: When Christians describe God as 'omniscient', they mean God is:
options: All-powerful
All-knowing
Outside of time
Everywhere at once
questions.explain: Omniscient means God knows everything, including all that has happened and will happen.

questions.q: According to Christian belief, Jesus' resurrection means he:
options: Rose to life again on the third day after his crucifixion
Was never really dead
Was replaced by another man
Appeared only as a ghost
questions.explain: Christians believe Jesus rose bodily from death on the third day after his crucifixion.

questions.q: For most Christians, the crucifixion is significant because Jesus':
options: Death paid the price for human sin (a sacrifice)
Escaped death at the last moment
Proved the Romans were just
Showed he was an ordinary teacher
questions.explain: Christians believe Jesus' death on the cross was a sacrifice that paid the price for human sin.

questions.q: The 'problem of evil' challenges Christians because it asks how:
options: Evil can be enjoyable
Heaven and hell can both exist
A good, all-powerful God can allow suffering
Humans invented religion
questions.explain: The problem of evil questions how an omnipotent and benevolent God can permit evil and suffering.

questions.q: The Christian idea of God as 'eternal' means that God:
options: Has no beginning and no end
Lives for a very long time then dies
Was created before the universe
Only exists in heaven
questions.explain: Eternal means God has always existed and will always exist, with no beginning or end.

questions.q: In Christian teaching, 'atonement' means:
options: Earning heaven through good works alone
A festival held at Easter
The forgiving of debts between people
Jesus' death restoring the relationship between God and humanity
questions.explain: Atonement is the belief that Jesus' death repaired (made 'at one') the broken relationship between God and humans.

questions.q: In John's Gospel, 'the Word' (Logos) refers to:
options: The Ten Commandments
The Bible itself
Jesus, who was with God and was God
The preaching of the prophets
questions.explain: John's Gospel calls Jesus the Word (Logos) who was with God and was God from the beginning.

questions.q: Which set of qualities best describes the Christian nature of God?
options: Omnipotent, benevolent and just
Distant, uncaring and changeable
Limited, sometimes unfair
Physical, mortal and visible
questions.explain: Christians believe God is omnipotent (all-powerful), benevolent (all-loving) and just (fair).

questions.q: In Christian belief, the Trinity describes God as:
options: Three persons in one God: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
A God who became three after Jesus died
One God who appears in three different moods
Three separate gods working together
questions.explain: The Trinity is the belief in one God existing as three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: In Christianity, 'salvation' refers to:
options: The first book of the Bible
A medieval monastery
A type of church service
Being saved from sin and given eternal life with God
questions.explain: Salvation is being saved from sin and its consequences, gaining eternal life with God.

questions.q: In Christianity, 'grace' is best understood as:
options: God's undeserved love and forgiveness freely given
The skill of living a holy life
A reward earned by attending church
A prayer said before meals only
questions.explain: Grace is God's free, unearned love and forgiveness offered to humanity.
